rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a pleasant or unpleasant smell.

example.english: This soup has a lovely smell.
example.traditional: 呢碗湯有陣好香嘅味道。
example.jyutping: ni1 wun2 tong1 jau5 zan6 hou2 hoeng1 ge3 mei6 dou6

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose way to say that something has a smell, including a figurative hint of a quality.

example.english: This coffee has a smell with a hint of chocolate.
example.traditional: 呢杯咖啡有味道，飲落有陣朱古力香。
example.jyutping: ni1 bui1 gaa3 fe1 jau5 mei6 dou6 jam2 lok6 jau5 zan6 zyu1 gu2 lik6 hoeng1

rows.note: Use 聞 for actively smelling or sensing an odour; it can also mean detecting something by smell.

example.english: I can smell a lovely aroma coming from the kitchen.
example.jyutping: ngo5 man4 dou2 cyu4 fong2 jau5 zan6 hoeng1 mei6

rows.note: A speaker uses this for a suspicious sign, especially in the expression 有蹺.

example.english: This deal seems strange; I smell something fishy.
example.traditional: 呢單嘢咁古怪，我覺得有蹺。
example.jyutping: ni1 daan1 je5 gam3 gu2 gwaai3 ngo5 gok3 dak1 jau5 kiu1

rows.note: Use this specifically when something has a bad or foul smell.

example.english: The rubbish has been sitting for two days, and now it has a bad smell.
example.traditional: 啲垃圾放咗兩日，而家有臭味喇。
example.jyutping: di1 laap6 saap3 fong3 zo2 loeng5 jat6 ji4 gaa1 jau5 cau3 mei6 laa3

rows.note: This refers specifically to the physical sense that detects smells.

example.english: That dog has a very keen sense of smell.
example.jyutping: zek3 gau2 ge3 cau3 gok3 hou2 ling4 man5

rows.note: Use this when you detect or figure something out specifically through its smell.

example.english: I could smell that someone was making soup as soon as I walked in.
example.traditional: 我一入門就聞出嚟有人煲緊湯。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jat1 jap6 mun4 zau6 man4 ceot1 lei4 jau5 jan4 bou1 gan2 tong1
